title: CITIBANK SHITTY BANK don't open an account with these fuckers SCAM!
description: I have thousands of dollars in my Citibank account, they stopped my DEBIT Card a month ago saying that it is compromised on their end.  Since then I have called them more than 13 times spending each time more than one hour of my life to arrange a card delivery but they always failed to do it,  not sending it at all, or sending it to the wrong address or sending it too late to a place where I was not anymore although I informed them my precise schedule.  Yesterday I went in person to the Citibank office in Brazil to get cash for my travel so that I can pay bills that cannot be paid by credit.  They made me waste almost 3 hours of my vacation in Rio de Janeiro  see if I was eligible to receive emergency cash and after that they said it is too late in the United States bank is already closed and they cannot do it so I should come back on Monday.  I do this on purpose every time I travel they are trying to stop me using my money instead they are using my money for their purposes.  I have thousands of dollars that I have no access to.  What is their job ?  Give me my fucking cash When I need it!   It's not a loan, it is a DEBIT CARD, this is real cash sitting in my account .  Worst of all I spent hours & hours of my vacation with them on the phone wasting my life with this piece of shit of scammers!  And so it happens I talk to people who had the same experience !! JUST AVOID CITIBANK USA!! Now GUESS WHAT!! I come back home, and there's money missing from my account! The money that I attempted to get over the counter in Brazil and they didn't want to give them to me, in fact they stole that amount from my funds and I had to call and tell them that I work for the media and will make a CNN report on them, and then they repatriated my funds in a day!

And what I have to tell you, it's not that easy. Like every time I spent one hour talking to Citibank using Wi-Fi through Skype from where I am, like on the street, they make you tell all your numbers, your mother's maiden name, your first school. So if somebody would sit next to me, could just note all my information yeah. And they take one hour to get all this information out of you, they put you on hold. In this holding time your connection is going to be stopped then you have to call again. You get the totally new person you have to explain everything then they go to connect you to other... to a higher employee so it is just on purpose, if they do this on purpose.. I tried to times to get the card so in Germany it didn't work out, now I'm in Brazil..like in Europe there was no Citibank so I couldn't go to an actual Citibank. I'm now in Brazil, next to my hotel there is a Citibank so I couldn't go to an actual Citibank. In Brazil, next to my hotel, there is a Citibank. I go there yesterday with all my documents, all my papers, because I need cash, you know. I have thousands of dollars in my Citibank account and I need that money, cash to give tips to people, to pay stuff that you cannot pay by credit card. so I go to the Citibank. what do you think they keep for two hours? calling back and forth to United States like if I'm eligible to to get my fxcking money out of this fxcking piece of sh!t of a bank! I mean that is their duty me as a customer I'm keeping thousands of dollars in my account their duty is just to give me my keeping thousands of dollars in my account their duty is just to give me my money when i fucking need it but no shitty bang shitty bang like really people get away from this scam because they do it on purpose like they knew i'm going to travel they knew i'm going to spend a lot of money and they cut it and every time, even here at the bank in Brazil, they were on the phone and after two hours of wasting my vacation time in —look where I am— in Rio de Janeiro, where yesterday it was really fucking beautiful weather, staying two hours in a fucking city bank, the guy finally says, today, but if you come on Monday, what the f**k? what the f**k is this piece of s**t of a bank? and I was speaking, you know, with other people in the hotel and everybody was saying they had same problems and one guy was saying that his wife also call the bank in advance that please, I'm gonna travel, do not cancel my card and that's what they do so people you should just stay away because this is a scam they do it on purpose they have my thousands of dollars so I was traveling for one month and I couldn't use my money because they fucked up on purpose and I have to use other banks money and in this time they are playing with my money. They make actually profit. So, just stay away of it and I'm going to follow on this and actually, I recorded conversations so I'm going to make videos with their conversation because this is just a huge rip-off. So people, be warned, Citibank should be renamed Shithibank because it's just a piece of a sheet of a bank. So that's all for now.

textual.observation: The speaker reports that Citibank disabled or failed to deliver a debit card while the speaker was traveling, leaving thousands of dollars in the account inaccessible and requiring repeated calls and an in-person visit to seek cash.

evidence.quote: they stopped my DEBIT Card a month ago saying that it is compromised on their end
I have thousands of dollars that I have no access to.
I go there yesterday with all my documents, all my papers, because I need cash

textual.context: Presented as a first-person complaint and warning about the bank; the speaker alleges intentional conduct, but intent is not independently established by these records.
textual.potential_relevance: The reported restriction on access to account funds is linked to repeated contact, travel-related cash needs, and an in-person attempt to obtain money, creating a concrete alleged mechanism for later review.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish why the card was restricted, whether the delivery failures were intentional, whether the account balance or access problem was independently verified, or whether any loss occurred.

textual.observation: The description reports that money corresponding to a cash request in Brazil was missing from the account after the bank did not provide the cash, and says the funds were later returned after the speaker threatened media reporting.

textual.limitations: The records do not establish whether the amount was actually debited, what transaction or authorization caused it, whether the funds were later restored, or whether the speaker's account of events is accurate.

Recording conversations for later videos further supports a reporting or consumer-warning context.
